subskill: Markup followed by a percent discount
grade_rationale: High for grade 7 (7.RP.A.3): two percent changes applied in sequence to different bases. The student must apply the 25% discount to the marked-up price, not to the cost and not by combining the percents. Grade-7 students commonly combine 60% and 25% into one 35% change or stop after the markup.
prompt: A store pays $54 for a jacket. The store marks up the price by 60% to set its selling price. During a sale, the store takes 25% off the selling price. What is the sale price of the jacket, in dollars?
explanation: The markup is 60% of $54, which is $32.40, so the selling price is $54 + $32.40 = $86.40. The discount is 25% of $86.40, which is $21.60, so the sale price is $86.40 - $21.60 = $64.80.

plugback.why: An option cannot be checked without running both percent changes forward; there is no single inverse step.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. Errors fall on both sides: subtracting 25 dollars is below the key; combining the percents and discounting only the markup are above.
intermediate_check: Solved intermediates 86.4 (selling price), 32.4 (markup) and 21.6 (discount) are not options. The "stops after the markup" error (86.4) was removed in the return because it is exactly key / 0.75.
cheap_bound_check: "Below the selling price" needs the selling price (86.4) computed and every option is below it anyway; "above the cost" is not a valid rule in general but every option is above 54, so it strikes nothing either way.
shape_check: All options are dollar amounts with one decimal place, between 54 and 86.4.
interior_parity_check: Middle values 64.8 and 72.9: both one-decimal amounts; the key is not cleaner.
dup_search: Probed earlier MAP items for "mark up", "markup", "marked up": none. Re-run through math-check near-duplicate against live ISEE/SSAT and every earlier MAP item after the return.
self_audit: Revision after screen pass 1 (S-R7: 57.6 & 76.8 differ by x0.75, the printed 25% off; 76.8 was the "stops after the markup" error, which is ALWAYS key / 0.75, so it was removed rather than renumbered). New error set: 1.6C - 25 (below), 1.35C (combined percents), C + 0.75 x 0.6C = 1.45C (discount taken off the markup only). Cost changed 48 -> 54 because at 48 the pair 51.8 & 64.8 is x1.251, close to the printed 25%. Key recomputed 54 x 1.6 x 0.75 = 64.8, rank 2. Every option pair checked for ratios 0.75, 1.25, 1.6, 1.35, 4/3, 0.6, 0.4, 2, 3, 4, 1.5, 10 and differences 25, 54, 60: none (ratios 1.125, 1.208, 1.074, 1.055, 1.187, 1.275). Key not a midpoint (61.4+72.9=134.3, 61.4+78.3=139.7, 72.9+78.3=151.2 vs 129.6) and no arithmetic run through it. Residual, stated for the screener: 78.3 - 64.8 = 13.5 = 25% of $54 and 72.9 - 64.8 = 8.1 = 15% of $54; both are inherent to those errors (1.45C - 1.2C, 1.35C - 1.2C) and need 25% or 15% of the cost computed, neither is a printed operation on an option, and neither singles out the key (the same 0.25C gap reading would equally support 78.3 as the answer).

78.3.misconception: takes the 25% off the markup only, as if the sale gives back part of the store's markup, not part of the selling price

subskill: Initial value of a linear function from two input-output pairs
grade_rationale: Mid for grade 8 (8.F.B.4): the student finds the rate from two data points and works back to the value at 0 hours. Grade-8 students often stop at the rate, give the difference in cost, or subtract only one hour of the rate.
prompt: A plumber charges a fixed fee for each visit plus the same amount for each hour of work. A 3-hour job costs $310, and a 5-hour job costs $390. What is the fixed fee, in dollars?
explanation: Two more hours cost $390 - $310 = $80, so each hour costs $80 / 2 = $40. Three hours cost 3 x $40 = $120, so the fixed fee is $310 - $120 = $190.
quantity_asked: the fixed fee in dollars (the value at 0 hours)

plugback.why: A fee option can be checked by adding 3 or 5 hours of the computed rate, but the rate must be found first.

structure_check: No bound or extremum. Errors fall on both sides: the rate and the difference are below the key; the one-hour subtraction is above.
intermediate_check: 40 and 80 are options: 80 is the difference of totals (solved first) and 40 the rate; both are named partial or wrong-variable errors in distractor_meta.
cheap_bound_check: The fee is less than $310 (the 3-hour cost); every option is below 310, so it strikes nothing.
shape_check: All options are whole dollar amounts.
interior_parity_check: Middle values 80 and 190; both multiples of 10, the key not cleaner.
dup_search: Probed earlier MAP Operations items for 'fixed fee', 'per hour', 'plus': no two-point initial-value item.
self_audit: Key recomputed: rate 40, fee 310 - 120 = 190; check 190 + 5 x 40 = 390.

40.misconception: gives the hourly rate instead of the fixed fee

80.misconception: gives the cost of the two extra hours (the difference in totals)

270.misconception: subtracts only one hour of the rate from the 3-hour cost
